commitResults.messageBody:
Dash.main mixed the user-input loop with task creation, listing, and completion updates. That made the high-level control flow harder to scan.

Extract focused command, list, add, and status handlers so main expresses session flow while each helper has a single responsibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class to handle user interactions
commitResults.messageBody:
User input reading and console message formatting are currently embedded
directly in the main Dash class. This mixes user interface concerns
with task management and program flow.

Extract a dedicated Ui class in the dash package to encapsulate all
user interactions, including greetings, prompt reading, divider lines,
status messages, and error reporting. Refactor Dash to instantiate Ui
and delegate all console I/O operations to it.

This establishes a clear separation between the presentation layer and
core chatbot logic, serving as the first step toward modular OOP
components.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Storage class to handle file persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
File reading, task serialization, directory creation, and task
deserialization are currently implemented directly inside Dash.
This tangles file persistence concerns with chatbot execution flow.

Extract a dedicated Storage class in the dash package to encapsulate
loading and saving tasks from the specified file path. Update Dash to
initialize and delegate task persistence to Storage.

This separates the storage layer from the application controller and
moves the codebase closer to the target object-oriented design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store deadline dates as LocalDate objects
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines currently store their due date as an unparsed String. This
prevents date validation, prevents date formatting, and precludes
future date-based operations like sorting or filtering.

Update Deadline to store its due date as a java.time.LocalDate and
format it as 'MMM dd yyyy' on display. Update Dash to parse deadline
dates from user input using the 'yyyy-MM-dd' format, rejecting invalid
dates with an informative error message. Update Storage to persist and
deserialize deadlines using ISO-8601 dates. Update test/ui-test-plan.md
to cover the new date format.

This improves type safety and provides standardized date presentation
across the application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add on command to filter tasks occurring on date
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines now store LocalDate instances, but the application lacks the
ability to query or filter tasks by date.

Add an occursOn(LocalDate) method to Task, overridden by Deadline to
check for matching due dates and by Event to check if a date falls
within its range. Introduce the 'on <yyyy-mm-dd>' command in Dash to
filter and print tasks occurring on a specified date using Ui. Add
Test 5 to test/ui-test-plan.md covering valid queries, empty results,
and malformed dates.

This enhances date utilization with polymorphic date filtering across
different task types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can currently list tasks or filter by date, but cannot search
tasks by keyword in the description.

Add a containsKeyword(String) method to Task for case-insensitive
matching. Add showMatchingTasks(List<Task>) to Ui to display matching
tasks or report when no matches exist. Introduce the 'find <keyword>'
command in Dash to search task descriptions and validate input. Update
test/ui-test-plan.md with Test 6 to verify the find command.

This allows users to quickly locate tasks matching a search term.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add header comments to non-trivial private methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Non-private classes and methods have header comments, but non-trivial
private helper methods in Dash and Storage lack Javadoc comments.

Add descriptive English Javadoc header comments to all non-trivial
private methods in Dash and Storage, describing method behavior,
parameters, return values, and thrown exceptions in accordance with the
SE-EDU Java coding standard. Wrap long lines to stay within 110
characters.

This improves code readability and satisfies the documentation standard
consistently across all classes.

The user documentation in docs/README.md previously contained only
placeholder comments.

Create a comprehensive and user-friendly User Guide covering quick
start instructions, all 10 supported commands with syntax and output
examples, automatic data storage behavior, and a command summary table
for quick reference.

This provides clear guidance for all application features while
remaining concise and easy to read.
